back: The stages a program passes through: analysis, design, coding, testing, maintenance.
Preliminary investigation, feasibility study, analysis, design, development, testing, implementation, maintenance, evaluation.
The stages are carried out once, in order; each is finished and approved before the next starts.
Benefits: simple, clear documents, easy to measure. Drawbacks: users see it late, changes are costly, testing is late.
Repeated cycles that each produce a working version, reviewed and improved in the next cycle.
Benefits: early working software, handles change, early risks. Drawbacks: cost and date harder to predict, needs user contact.
Quick development using prototypes built with users and reused components, refined into the final system.
Stable requirements: waterfall. Changing or unclear: iterative. Speed with available users: RAD.
It gives a plan, documents and checkpoints, so a project is predictable and the system meets the user's needs.
